dataList.content:
啊，小布布……这是鞋子，吾想。
 Ah, Young Pwie... These are shoes, I believe.

它们护汝双足免受伤痛……挡住风雪与寒风……使嬉戏玩耍成为一桩乐事。诚然，每位冒险者都该穿一双结实的鞋。
 They shield thy soles from pain... keep out the snow and rain and bitter wind... and make frolicking about a most joyous thing. Forsooth, every adventurer ought to wear a stout pair of shoes.

这些鞋能让饥饿消失吗？
 Will these shoes make the hunger go away?

……不，吾并不惧怕。
 ... Nay, I fear not.

诚然，忍受那份渴望——不，那份饥饿——是桩艰苦的考验。故而……吾始终不懈地压抑着这股冲动。
 Verily, 'tis a grievous trial to endure the yearning—nay, hunger. Wherefore... I labor to suppress the urge without end.

压抑这股冲动有什么好处？
 What's good about suppressing the urge?

其一，汝之冒险将不致蒙羞，而会化作汝无需羞于诉说的故事……
 For one, thine adventure shall remain unmarred, and become tales thou shan't be ashamed to tell...

……借此，汝方能梦见汝所渴望成为的、未来的自己。
 ... through which thou mayest dream of the future self thou seekest to become.

终有一日，汝将毫无愧色地，向那愿聆听汝一切经历的人，诉说汝的冒险。
 And someday, thou wilt, without suffering dishonor, tell all about thine adventures to another soul who shall heed thine accounts.

我想成为的自己……
 The self I want to become...

布布久久凝视着那双鞋……
 Pwie stared at the shoes for a long while...

缓缓走上前去，最终把鞋穿上了脚。
 And approached them slowly, before finally slipping them on.

如今便踏着属于汝自己的鞋，以更饱满的气力继续前行吧！
 Now march onward with greater vigor, astride shoes of thine own!

<也许只是我的错觉，默尔索……>
 <This might just be me, Meursault...>

<但你不觉得……布布最近跟我们跟得比以前更紧了吗？>
 <But don't you think... Pwie's started to follow us more closely than before?>
